taxonomic_note: Accepted Tragia nigricans Bush; current Kew/POWO treatment places its native range in south-central Texas.
look_here_first: Use the erect dark purple-green to reddish-black stem together with oblong to oblanceolate coarsely serrate leaves and the very small terminal or leaf-opposed raceme. Confirm with flower counts, pedicel bases, and capsule size rather than stem color alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kendall and Bandera are explicitly documented in Texas Parks & Wildlife annotated rare-species county material; Kerr is locked by E. J. Palmer 33811 collected near Kerrville on 7 May 1928.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not infer Hays County from source-pool membership or from the broader south-central Texas native range.

best_field_traits: erect stems purple-green to reddish black, apex not flexuous
oblong to oblanceolate leaves with coarse serration
persistent staminate pedicel bases about 0.2–0.4 mm
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Dark erect stems help, but leaf base, raceme structure, flower count, pedicel bases, and mature capsule are required for confident separation.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Dark erect stems help, but leaf base, raceme structure, flower count, pedicel bases, and mature capsule are required for confident separation.
